title.en: Volume 55 Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, F Long
title.raw: 卷五十五 列傳第十五 臧燾 徐廣 傅隆 Volume 55 Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, F Long

sentences.zh: 列傳第十五 臧燾徐廣傅隆

translations.literal: Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, and Fu Long

sentences.zh: 臧燾，字德仁，東莞莒人，武敬皇后兄也。

translations.literal: Zang Dao, styled Deren, was a man of Ju in Dongguan, elder brother of Empress Jingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dao, courtesy name Deren, came from Ju in Dongguan and was the elder brother of Empress Jingwu.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善《三禮》，貧約自立，操行為鄉里所稱。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; poor and self-restrained, his conduct was praised in his village.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; though poor, he supported himself, and his conduct was praised throughout his district.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元中，衛將軍謝安始立國學，徐、兗二州刺史謝玄舉燾為助教。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era of Jin Emperor Xiaowu, General of the Guard Xie An first established the National University; the Xu and Yan inspectors Xie Xuan recommended Dao as Assistant Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, General of the Guard Xie An first established the National University, and Xie Xuan, inspector of Xu and Yan provinces, recommended Dao as assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝追崇庶祖母宣太后，議者或謂宜配食中宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously honored his common grandmother Empress Dowager Xuan; some debaters held she should share sacrifice with Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously honored his common grandmother, Empress Dowager Xuan; some debaters held that she should share sacrifices with Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 燾議曰：「《陽秋》，之義，母以子貴，故仲子、成風，咸稱夫人。

translations.literal: Dao argued: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that the mother is honored through the son; therefore Zhongzi and Chengfeng are both called lady.
translations.idiomatic: Dao argued: "The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that a mother is honored through her son; therefore both Zhongzi and Chengfeng were styled lady.

sentences.zh: 《經》雲'考仲子之宮'。

translations.literal: The classic says, 'Examine Zhongzi's palace.'
translations.idiomatic: The classic says, 'Examine Zhongzi's palace.'

sentences.zh: 若配食惠廟，則宮無緣別築。

translations.literal: If she shared sacrifice at Duke Hui's temple, the palace would have no reason to be built separately.
translations.idiomatic: If she were to share sacrifices at Duke Hui's temple, there would be no occasion to build a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 前漢孝文、孝昭太后，並系子為號，祭於寢園，不配于高祖、孝武之廟。

translations.literal: Former Han's Empress Dowagers Xiaowen and Xiaozhao both took their titles from their sons and were sacrificed in the tomb park, not sharing the temples of Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowagers Xiaowen and Xiaozhao of Former Han both took their titles from their sons and were sacrificed in the tomb park, not sharing the temples of Emperors Gaozu and Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 後漢和帝之母曰恭懷皇所，安帝祖母曰敬隱皇后，順帝之母曰恭湣皇后，雖不系子為號，亦祭於陵寢。

translations.literal: Later Han's Empress Gonghuai, mother of Emperor He; Empress Jingyin, grandmother of Emperor An; and Empress Gongmin, mother of Emperor Shun — though not taking their titles from their sons, were also sacrificed at the tomb parks.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's Empress Gonghuai, mother of Emperor He; Empress Jingyin, grandmother of Emperor An; and Empress Gongmin, mother of Emperor Shun — though they did not take their titles from their sons, were likewise sacrificed at the tomb parks.

sentences.zh: 不配章、安二帝。

translations.literal: They did not share sacrifice with Emperors Zhang and An.
translations.idiomatic: They did not share sacrifices with Emperors Zhang and An.

sentences.zh: 此則二漢雖有太后、皇后之異，至於並不配食，義同《陽秋》。

translations.literal: Thus though the two Han dynasties differed in whether they were empress dowagers or empresses, as to not sharing sacrifice at all, the meaning matches the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, although the two Han dynasties differed as to whether the honoree was an empress dowager or an empress, in neither case did they share sacrifice — the principle agrees with the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 唯光武追廢呂後，故以薄後配高祖廟。

translations.literal: Only Guangwu posthumously deposed Empress Lü, and therefore Empress Bo shared Emperor Gaozu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guangwu posthumously deposed Empress Lü, and therefore Empress Bo was paired with Emperor Gaozu in his temple.

sentences.zh: 又衛後既廢，霍光追尊李夫人為皇后，配孝武廟，此非母以子貴之例，直以高、武二廟無配故耳。

translations.literal: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and she shared Emperor Xiaowu's temple — this is not the case of the mother honored through the son, but simply because the temples of Gaozu and Xiaowu had no consort.
translations.idiomatic: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and paired her with Emperor Xiaowu in his temple — this was not a case of the mother honored through the son, but simply because the temples of Gaozu and Xiaowu had no consort.

sentences.zh: 夫漢立寢於陵，自是晉制所異。

translations.literal: As for Han establishing tomb chambers at the mausoleums, that differs from Jin practice.
translations.idiomatic: Han established tomb chambers at the mausoleums — this already differed from Jin practice.

sentences.zh: 謂宜遠准《陽秋》考宮之義，近摹二漢不配之典。

translations.literal: I hold that one should follow afar the Spring and Autumn meaning of examining the palace, and near emulate the two Han canon of not sharing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that one should follow the distant precedent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in examining the palace, and take as a near model the two Han canon of not sharing sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尊號既正，則罔極之情申，別建寢廟，則嚴禰之義顯，系子為稱，兼明母貴之所由，一舉而允三義，固哲王之高致也。

translations.literal: Once the honored title is correct, boundless filial feeling is expressed; if a separate tomb-chamber temple is built, the principle of honoring the near ancestors is clear; taking the title from the son also clarifies whence the mother's honor comes — one act satisfies three meanings; truly the lofty aim of a sage king.
translations.idiomatic: Once the honored title is settled, boundless filial feeling is expressed; if a separate tomb-chamber temple is built, the principle of honoring father and mother in their proper stations is clear; taking one's title from one's son also clarifies whence a mother's honor arises — one act satisfies three meanings; this is truly the lofty aim of a sage king.

sentences.zh: 」議者從之。

translations.literal: " The debaters followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The debaters followed his view.

sentences.zh: 頃之，去官。

translations.literal: Before long he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 以母老家貧，與弟熹俱棄人事，躬耕自業，約己養親者十餘載。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old and the family poor, he and his younger brother Xi together abandoned worldly affairs, plowing for themselves and restraining their lives to nourish their kin for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was old and the family poor, he and his younger brother Xi together withdrew from public life, plowed the fields themselves, and for more than ten years lived frugally to support their parents.

sentences.zh: 父母喪亡，居喪六年，以毀瘠著稱。

translations.literal: When his parents died, he observed mourning for six years and was famed for grief-wasting.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died, he observed mourning for six years and was famed for the emaciation of his grief.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除臨沂令。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，為太學博士，參右將軍何無忌軍事，隨府轉鎮南參軍。

translations.literal: When the banner of righteousness was raised, he became Doctor of the National University, joined Right General He Wuji's staff, and followed the headquarters to Staff Officer of Pacifying the South.
translations.idiomatic: When the banner of righteousness was raised, he became a doctor of the National University, joined the staff of Right General He Wuji, and followed the headquarters to staff officer of Pacifying the South.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮京口，與燾書曰：「頃學尚廢弛，後進頹業，衡門之內，清風輟響。

translations.literal: When Gaozu garrisoned Jingkou, he wrote to Dao: "Recently learning has been neglected and the younger generation's work has declined; within the humble gate, the pure wind has ceased to resound.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu garrisoned Jingkou, he wrote to Dao: "Learning has lately fallen into neglect, and the younger generation's work has declined; within humble households the pure wind of scholarship has ceased to sound.

sentences.zh: 良由戎車屢警，禮樂中息，浮夫恣志，情與事染，豈可不敷崇墳籍，敦厲風尚。

translations.literal: Truly because war-chariots have repeatedly alerted and ritual and music have paused in the midst, floating men indulge their will and feeling is stained by affairs — how can one not broadly promote the classics and earnestly encourage custom?
translations.idiomatic: This is surely because war-chariots have repeatedly sounded the alarm and ritual and music have halted midway; drifting men indulge their whims and feeling is stained by affairs — how can we fail to spread the classics broadly and earnestly revive custom?

sentences.zh: 此境人士，子侄如林，明發搜訪，想聞令軌。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of this region have nephews like a forest; if one searches openly, one hopes to hear of proper models.
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of this region have sons and nephews thick as a forest; search them out openly, and I trust we shall hear of worthy models.

sentences.zh: 然荊玉含寶，要俟開瑩，幽蘭懷馨，事資扇發，獨習寡悟，義著周典。

translations.literal: Yet jade of Jing contains treasure and must wait to be opened and polished; orchids in the deep hold fragrance and depend on being fanned awake; solitary study with little awakening — the meaning appears in the Zhou canon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet jade of Jing holds its treasure and must wait to be cut and polished; orchids in the deep hold their fragrance and depend on being stirred awake; solitary study with little awakening — the meaning is set forth in the Zhou canon.

sentences.zh: 今經師不遠，而赴業無聞，非唯志學者鮮，或是勸誘未至邪。

translations.literal: Now the classical masters are not far, yet none are heard going to pursue learning — not only are aspirants few, but perhaps encouragement has not yet arrived?
translations.idiomatic: Now the masters of the classics are not far away, yet no one is heard going to pursue learning — is it not only that aspirants are few, but perhaps encouragement has not yet reached them?

sentences.zh: 想複弘之。

translations.literal: I trust you will also promote it.
translations.idiomatic: I trust you will also promote it."

sentences.zh: 」參高祖中軍軍事，入補尚書度支郎，改掌祠部。

translations.literal: " He joined Gaozu's central army staff, entered to fill the post of Gentleman of the Revenue Department in the Secretariat, and changed to control the Sacrifices Department.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Gaozu's central army staff, entered the Secretariat as gentleman of the revenue department, and was reassigned to head the sacrifices department.

sentences.zh: 襲封高陵亭侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Gaoling district.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Gaoling district.

sentences.zh: 時太廟鴟尾災，燾謂著作郎徐廣曰：「昔孔子在齊，聞魯廟災，曰必桓、僖也。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial temple's owl-tail finial burned; Dao told Compiler Xu Guang, "Formerly when Confucius was in Qi and heard of the Lu temple's disaster he said it must be Huan and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time fire destroyed the owl-tail finials of the imperial ancestral temple. Dao said to compiler Xu Guang, "When Confucius was in Qi and heard that the Lu temple had burned, he said it must concern Duke Huan and Duke Xi.

sentences.zh: 今征西、京兆四府君，宜在毀落，而猶列廟饗，此其征乎？

translations.literal: Now the four lords of Pacifying the West and Jingzhao should be in the falling line and yet still stand in the temple sacrifices — is this not the sign?
translations.idiomatic: Now the four lords of Pacifying the West and Jingzhao ought to be in the line for removal, yet they still stand in the temple sacrifices — is this not the omen?"

sentences.zh: 」乃上議曰：「臣聞國之大事，在祀與戎，將營宮室，宗廟為首。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the state's great affairs are sacrifice and war; when planning palace chambers, the ancestral temple comes first.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that the great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war, and that when one is about to build palace chambers, the ancestral temple comes first.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，莫不致肅恭之誠心，盡崇嚴乎祖考，然後能流淳化于四海，通幽感於神明。

translations.literal: Ancient sage kings all showed reverent sincerity and utmost honor toward ancestors and fathers, and only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and hidden feeling reach the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity all showed reverent sincerity and rendered utmost honor to their ancestors and fathers; only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and hidden feeling reach the spirits.

sentences.zh: 固宜詳廢興於古典，循情禮以求中者也。

translations.literal: One should indeed examine abolition and establishment in ancient canon and seek the mean through feeling and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: One should indeed examine abolition and establishment against ancient canon and seek the mean through feeling and ritual.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖而七。

translations.literal: Ritual: the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao three mu, with the Grand Ancestor making seven.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao and three mu, with the Grand Ancestor making seven.

sentences.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之，遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。

translations.literal: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice; the distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.
translations.idiomatic: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice; the distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.

sentences.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之。

translations.literal: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; when there is prayer, then sacrifice is made.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; only when there is prayer is sacrifice made.

sentences.zh: 此宗廟之次，親疏之序也。

translations.literal: This is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: This is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far kin.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王、武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

sentences.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。

translations.literal: Examining the words "beyond tiao," then tiao are not the temples of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: If one examines the phrase "beyond tiao," then tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 文、武周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？

translations.literal: Wen and Wu were Zhou's ancestors — how can one speak of beyond tiao as altar?
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu were Zhou's founding ancestors — how could one speak of "beyond tiao" as reaching the altar?

sentences.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。

translations.literal: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond the period of mourning.

sentences.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之禮，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者，其義彌疏也。

translations.literal: Again for distant temples there is the rite of offering and tasting; beyond tiao there is the difference of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation the more sparse the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Again, distant temples have the rites of offering and tasting, while beyond tiao there is the distinction of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation, the more attenuated the rite.

sentences.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。

translations.literal: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu they should like the Grand Ancestor receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is from the beginning of merit, not that the meaning of honor has difference and descent each time.
translations.idiomatic: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought, like the Grand Ancestor, to receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is because merit begins with him — it is not that the meaning of honor is graded downward each time.

sentences.zh: 又禮有以多貴者，故傳稱德厚者流光，德薄者流卑。

translations.literal: Again ritual has what values the many; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual also holds that abundance is honored; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."

sentences.zh: 又雲自上以下，降殺以兩，禮也。

translations.literal: Again it says from above to below reduction by twos — that is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that from above to below the reduction proceeds by twos — such is ritual.

sentences.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。

translations.literal: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text of difference above and below.
translations.idiomatic: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text that distinguishes above from below.

sentences.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet it says Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet it also says that Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — how can this be?

sentences.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫，而上祀之禮，不過高祖。

translations.literal: Again the king sacrifices for legitimate early-dead sons, extending down to coming generations, yet sacrifice by superiors does not exceed the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the king sacrifices for legitimate sons who died young, extending down to coming generations, yet the rite of sacrifice by superiors does not go beyond the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊屬，亦非聖人制禮之意也。

translations.literal: Pushing honor down the stream while replacing sincere reverence at the honored kin — this too is not the sage's intent in making ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To push honor down the stream while displacing sincere reverence owed to honored kin is likewise not the intent of the sages in establishing ritual.

sentences.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。

translations.literal: Therefore when Taishi established the temple they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father is a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice uses Son of Heaven and feudal lord while the corpse's garment uses knight's garment.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the Taishi temple was established, they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father was a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice was performed as for Son of Heaven or feudal lord while the corpse's garment was that of a knight.

sentences.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數，宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。

translations.literal: Thus upstream to Pacifying the West, to complete the number of six generations; Emperor Xuan though Grand Ancestor was still in the place of descendants; on the day of the great offering he had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is called though the son equals sainthood he does not eat before the father.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the line was carried up to Pacifying the West to complete the number of six generations; Emperor Xuan, though Grand Ancestor, was still in the place of descendants, and on the day of the great offering had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is meant by the saying that though the son equals sainthood, he does not eat before the father.

sentences.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨。

translations.literal: Now that Jingzhao and above have moved, the Grand Ancestor at last occupies the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not full, wish to bend the Grand Ancestor to the low seat — your servant holds this is not the intent of ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jingzhao and above have been moved out, the Grand Ancestor can at last occupy the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not yet full, wish to place the Grand Ancestor in the lower seat — your servant holds that this is not the intent of ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 所與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太祖在六世之外，非為須滿七廟，乃得居太祖也。

translations.literal: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" is itself that zhao and mu are already sufficient; the Grand Ancestor lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before he may occupy the place of Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" means that zhao and mu are already sufficient and the Grand Ancestor lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before he may occupy the place of Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 議者又以四府君神主宜永同于殷祫，臣又以為不然。

translations.literal: Debaters also held the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great offering like the yin sacrifice; your servant again holds this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters also held that the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great yin offering; your servant again holds that this is not so.

sentences.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。

translations.literal: Tradition speaks of the destroyed temple's tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition speaks of the tablets of destroyed temples being displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故《白虎通》雲'禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and hold the line without breaking.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move the tablets of destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and preserve the line without breaking it.

sentences.zh: 」豈如四府君在太祖之前乎。

translations.literal: " How could the four lords be before the Grand Ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: " How could the four lords stand before the Grand Ancestor?

sentences.zh: 非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基，昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍，未見其可。

translations.literal: They are not lords who continue the line, have no auspicious mandate, are not the foundation of royal enterprise; formerly because the generation was near they were included; now feeling and ritual are already far — yet they should long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts, one does not see that it may be done.
translations.idiomatic: They were not lords who continued the line, bore no auspicious mandate, and were not the foundation of royal enterprise; formerly they were included because the generation was near, but now feeling and ritual are already distant — yet they would long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts, one does not see how it can be justified.

sentences.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以淵儒碩學，鹹謂四府君神主，無緣永存於百世。

translations.literal: Formerly at the beginning of Yonghe there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound Confucian scholars, all held the four lords' spirit tablets had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghe era there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound Confucian scholars, all held that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所秉小異，而大歸是同。

translations.literal: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them — though what they held differed in small ways the great direction was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild temples for them — though their proposals differed in small ways, the great direction was the same.

sentences.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭，長無太祖之位矣。

translations.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.
translations.idiomatic: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.

sentences.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚；

translations.literal: Principle values the mean — one need not exceed in thickness;
translations.idiomatic: Principle values the mean, and one need not exceed in lavishness;

sentences.zh: 禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷！

translations.literal: ritual moves with the age — how can one follow without deciding!
translations.idiomatic: ritual moves with the age — how can one follow custom without deciding!

sentences.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈厲之諡彌彰；

translations.literal: Thus though the feeling of subject and son is sincere, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer;
translations.idiomatic: Thus though the feeling of subject and son may be deep, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer;

sentences.zh: 追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。

translations.literal: though the longing to reach the distant is keen, the ritual of moving and destroying temples is what applies.
translations.idiomatic: though the longing to reach the distant is keen, the ritual of moving and destroying temples is what must be applied.

sentences.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可逾爾。

translations.literal: Is it not that one has the heart to add thickness, yet ritual system cannot be exceeded?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that one wishes in one's heart to add further honor, yet ritual system cannot be exceeded?

sentences.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處，虞主所以依神，神移則有 瘞埋之禮。

translations.literal: A stone chamber means storing north of the temple; rebuilding means the place is not yet known; the provisional tablet exists to depend on the spirit — when the spirit moves there is the rite of burial.
translations.idiomatic: A stone chamber means storing the tablets north of the temple; rebuilding means the place is not yet known; the provisional tablet exists to lodge the spirit — when the spirit moves, there is the rite of burial.

sentences.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也，准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。

translations.literal: If the four lords' feasting sacrifice should be abolished, the spirits likewise do not depend on them; following parallel cases, it should be the same as burying the provisional tablet.
translations.idiomatic: If the feasting sacrifices to the four lords should be abolished, the spirits likewise no longer depend on them; following parallel cases, they should be treated like the burial of provisional tablets.

sentences.zh: 然經典難詳，群言紛錯，非臣卑淺所能折中。

translations.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail and many opinions are tangled — this is not what your servant's low shallowness can reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the classics are hard to detail fully and many opinions are tangled — this is not something your servant's lowly shallowness can reconcile.

sentences.zh: 」時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。

translations.literal: " At the time most scholars followed Dao's argument, but in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time most scholars followed Dao's argument, but in the end it was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 遷通直郎，高祖鎮軍、車騎、中軍、太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant, and served as advisory staff officer to Gaozu when he was General Who Garrisons the Army, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army, and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct attendant and served as advisory staff officer to Gaozu when the latter was General Who Garrisons the Army, General of Chariots and Cavalry, central army commander, and grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐關、洛，大司馬琅邪王同行，除大司馬從事中郎，總留府事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned north against Guan and Luo, the Grand Marshal Prince of Langye went with him; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman of the Grand Marshal and oversaw all affairs left at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu campaigned north against Guan and Luo, the grand marshal, Prince of Langye, went with him; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman of the grand marshal and oversaw all affairs left at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 義熙十四年，除侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 元熙元年，以腳疾去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi he left office because of foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxi he resigned because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，征拜太常，雖外戚貴顯，而彌自沖約，茅屋蔬餐，不改其舊。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the mandate he was summoned as Grand Minister of Ceremonies; though a noble maternal relative, he became all the more self-restrained — thatched hut and vegetable meals, not changing his former ways.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received the mandate, Dao was summoned as grand minister of ceremonies; though a noble maternal relative, he became all the more self-restrained — thatched hut and vegetable meals, unchanged from his former ways.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿，與親戚共之。

translations.literal: The salary he received he shared with kin.
translations.idiomatic: The salary he received he shared with his kin.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，致仕，拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he retired and was appointed grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，時年七十。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 少帝追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Shaodi posthumously honored him as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shaodi posthumously honored him as left grand master of splendid happiness and added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 長子邃，護軍司馬，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Sui was staff officer to the Protector of the Army and governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Sui served as staff officer to the protector of the army and as governor of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 少子綽，太子中舍人，新安太守。

translations.literal: His younger son Chuo was attendant gentleman of the heir apparent and governor of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Chuo served as attendant gentleman of the heir apparent and as governor of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 邃長子諶之，尚書都官郎，烏程令。

translations.literal: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi was gentleman of the Ministry of Justice's punishment section and magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi served as gentleman of the punishment section in the Ministry of Justice and as magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 諶之弟凝之，學涉有當世才具，與司空徐湛之為異常之交。

translations.literal: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was broadly learned and had talent for the age; with Minister of Works Xu Zhanzhi he had an extraordinary friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was broadly learned and possessed talent fit for the age; with Minister of Works Xu Zhanzhi he formed an extraordinary friendship.

sentences.zh: 年少時與北地傅僧祐俱以通家子始為太祖所引見，時上與何尚之論鑄錢事，凝之便幹其語，上因回與論之。

translations.literal: In youth he and Fu Shengyou of Beidi, both as sons of allied families, were first introduced to Emperor Taizu; at the time the emperor was debating coinage with He Shangzhi, and Ningzhi inserted himself into their talk, whereupon the emperor turned and debated with him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he and Fu Shengyou of Beidi, both sons of allied families, were first introduced to Emperor Taizu; at the time the emperor was debating coinage with He Shangzhi, and Ningzhi broke into their discussion, whereupon the emperor turned and debated with him.

sentences.zh: 僧祐引凝之衣令止，凝之大言謂僧祐曰：「明主難再遇，便應正盡所懷。

translations.literal: Shengyou pulled Ningzhi's garment to make him stop; Ningzhi spoke loudly to Shengyou: "An enlightened lord is hard to meet twice — one should straightway fully express what is in one's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Shengyou pulled Ningzhi's garment to make him stop, but Ningzhi said loudly to Shengyou, "An enlightened lord is hard to meet twice — one ought straightway to express fully what is in one's heart.

sentences.zh: 」上與往復十餘反，凝之詞韻銓序，兼有理證，上甚賞焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor and he went back and forth more than ten times; Ningzhi's words were measured in tone and order, with reasoning and proof together, and the emperor greatly admired this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor and he went back and forth more than ten times; Ningzhi's words were measured in tone and orderly in arrangement, with reasoning and proof together, and the emperor greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 曆隨王誕後軍記室錄事，欲以為青州，其事不果。

translations.literal: He served successively as recorder-clerk in the rear army staff office of Prince of Sui Wang Dan; they wished to make him governor of Qingzhou, but the matter did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as recorder-clerk on the rear army staff of Prince Dan of Sui; they wished to appoint him governor of Qingzhou, but the matter did not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞，以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat and, as a partisan of Xu Zhanzhi, was killed by the prime culprit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right assistant minister of the Secretariat and, as a partisan of Xu Zhanzhi, was killed by the prime culprit.

sentences.zh: 子夤，尚書主客郎，沈攸之征西功曹，為攸之盡節，事在《攸之傳》。

translations.literal: His son Yin was gentleman of the host-guest section in the Secretariat and merit officer on Pacifying the West staff under Shen Youzhi; he gave full loyalty to Youzhi — the affair is in Youzhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin served as gentleman of the host-guest section in the Secretariat and as merit officer on Pacifying the West staff under Shen Youzhi; he gave his full loyalty to Youzhi — the affair is recorded in Youzhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 凝之弟潭之，亦有美譽。

translations.literal: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi also had fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi also enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，曆尚書吏部郎，禦史中丞。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's reign he served successively as gentleman of the personnel section in the Secretariat and imperial censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Taizong he served successively as gentleman of the personnel section in the Secretariat and as imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，為左民尚書，卒官。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era of Emperor Houfei he was Left Minister of the People and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era of Emperor Houfei he served as left minister of the people and died in office.

sentences.zh: 潭之弟澄之，太子左積弩將軍。

translations.literal: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi was Left General of Stacked Crossbows of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi served as left general of stacked crossbows to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，領軍於盱眙，為索虜所破，見殺，追贈通直郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded the army at Xuyi, was defeated by the northern barbarians, and was killed; posthumously honored as Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded the army at Xuyi, was defeated by the northern barbarians, and was killed; he was posthumously honored as direct attendant.

sentences.zh: 綽子煥，順帝升明中，為武昌太守。

translations.literal: Chuo's son Huan, in the Shengming era of Emperor Shundi, was governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's son Huan, during the Shengming era of Emperor Shundi, served as governor of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之攻郢城，煥棄郡赴之；

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi attacked Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his commandery and went to join him;
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi attacked Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his commandery and went to join him;

sentences.zh: 攸之敗，伏誅。

translations.literal: when Youzhi was defeated, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: when Youzhi was defeated, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 傅僧祐，祖父弘仁，高祖外弟也。

translations.literal: Fu Shengyou — his grandfather Hongren was a maternal younger brother of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shengyou's grandfather Hongren was a maternal younger brother of Gaozu (Liu Yu).

sentences.zh: 以中表曆顯官，征虜將軍、南譙太守，太常卿。

translations.literal: Through marriage kinship he held successive prominent offices: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Administrator of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Through ties of marriage kinship he rose through prominent offices, serving as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Administrator of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 子邵，員外散騎侍郎，妻燾女也，生僧祐，有吏才，再為山陰令，甚有能名，末世令長莫及。

translations.literal: His son Shao was Supernumerary Attendant Cavalry Gentleman and married Zang Dao's daughter; he fathered Shengyou, who had talent for administration, twice served as magistrate of Shanyin, won a great reputation for competence, and at the end of the dynasty no county magistrate could match him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao was supernumerary attendant cavalry gentleman and married Zang Dao's daughter; Shengyou was born to them. He had a gift for administration, served twice as magistrate of Shanyin, and won such a reputation for competence that in the dynasty's last years no county magistrate could equal him.

sentences.zh: 亦以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: He was also killed by the Prince of Evil for being in Xu Yuanzhi's faction.
translations.idiomatic: He was also killed by the Prince of Evil (Liu Shao) as a member of Xu Yuanzhi's faction.

sentences.zh: 徐廣，字野民，東莞姑幕人也。

translations.literal: Xu Guang, styled Yemin, was a native of Gumu in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang, styled Yemin, was from Gumu in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 父藻，都水使者。

translations.literal: His father Zao was Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao was commissioner of waterways.

sentences.zh: 兄邈，太子前衛率。

translations.literal: His elder brother Miao was Forward Commander of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Miao was forward commander of the heir apparent's guard.

sentences.zh: 家世好學，至廣尤精，百家數術，無不研覽。

translations.literal: The family for generations loved learning; Guang was especially refined, and of the hundred schools and numerical arts there was none he did not study and examine.
translations.idiomatic: The family had loved learning for generations; Guang was especially accomplished, and among the hundred schools and numerical arts there was none he did not study.

sentences.zh: 謝玄為州，辟廣從事西曹。

translations.literal: When Xie Xuan was regional inspector, he recruited Guang as Western Bureau aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Xuan governed the province, he recruited Guang as western bureau aide.

sentences.zh: 又譙王司馬恬鎮北參軍。

translations.literal: He also served as Northern Campaign staff officer under Sima Tian, Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as northern campaign staff officer under Prince of Qiao Sima Tian.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝以廣博學，除為秘書郎，校書秘閣，增置職僚。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, because Guang was broadly learned, appointed him Secretary Gentleman; he collated books in the Secret Repository and additional staff were added.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, finding Guang broadly learned, made him secretariat gentleman; he collated books in the secret repository and staff were added.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎，領校書如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalry Gentleman, continuing to oversee collation as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supernumerary attendant cavalry gentleman, continuing to oversee collation as before.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，尚書令王珣舉為祠部郎。

translations.literal: In the Long'an era, Minister of the Interior Wang Xun recommended him as Senior Clerk of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an, Minister of the Interior Wang Xun recommended him as senior clerk of rites.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王世子元顯錄尚書，欲使百僚致敬，台內使廣立議，由是內外並執下官禮，廣常為愧恨焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Heir of Kuaiji, Sima Yuanxian, recorded the Ministry of the Interior and wished to make the hundred officials pay homage; the inner office had Guang establish the debate, and therefore inside and outside both observed the lower-official ritual — Guang was often ashamed and resentful of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuaiji's heir Sima Yuanxian recorded the interior and wished homage from all officials, Guang was made to establish the debate; inside and outside then held lower-official ritual — Guang was often ashamed and resentful.

sentences.zh: 元顯引為中軍參軍，遷領軍長史。

translations.literal: Yuanxian brought him in as Central Army staff officer and promoted him to chief clerk of the Palace Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian brought him in as central army staff officer and promoted him to chief clerk of the palace army.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，以為大將軍文學祭酒。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan held power, Guang was made Literary Libationer to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan held power, he was made literary libationer to the grand general.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，高祖使撰車服儀注，乃除鎮軍諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, Gaozu had him compile regulations for carriages, robes, and ritual, and appointed him Staff Adviser to the General Who Pacifies the Army, concurrently Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At Yixi's start Gaozu had him compile carriage, robe, and ritual regulations and appointed him staff adviser to the pacifying general, concurrently recorder.

sentences.zh: 封樂成縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Lecheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Lecheng county.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎常侍，領著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant and concurrently Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supernumerary regular cavalry attendant and concurrently compiler.

sentences.zh: 二年，尚書奏曰：「臣聞左史述言，右官書事，《乘》、《志》顯于晉、鄭，《陽秋》著乎魯史。

translations.literal: In the second year the Ministry of the Interior submitted, saying: "Your servant has heard that the left historian records speech and the right official records affairs; the Cheng and Zhi are illustrious in Jin and Zheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals stand forth in the Lu chronicle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the interior memorialized: "Your servant has heard that the left historian records speech and the right official records affairs; the Cheng and Zhi shine in Jin and Zheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals stand forth in Lu's chronicle.

sentences.zh: 自皇代有造，中興晉祀，道風帝典，煥乎史策。

translations.literal: Since the imperial age was founded and Jin's sacrifices were revived, the Way and wind of the imperial canon have shone brilliantly in the historical registers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial age was founded and Jin's sacrifices revived, the Way and wind of the imperial canon have shone brilliantly in the historical registers.

sentences.zh: 而太和以降，世曆三朝，玄風聖跡，倏為疇古。

translations.literal: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed, and the mysterious wind and sage traces have suddenly become the distant past.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed, and sage traces have suddenly become the distant past.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳，宜敕著作郎徐廣撰成國史。

translations.literal: Your servants have examined the matter in detail and hold that Compiler Xu Guang should be ordered to complete the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants hold that Compiler Xu Guang should be ordered to complete the national history.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「先朝至德光被，未著方策，宜流風緬代，永貽將來者也。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "The former dynasty's supreme virtue spread its radiance but has not been set down in the registers; its flowing wind should reach across generations and be bequeathed forever to those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict said: "The former dynasty's supreme virtue spread its radiance but has not been set down in the registers; its flowing wind should reach across generations and be bequeathed to those who come after.

sentences.zh: 便敕撰集。」

translations.literal: Let compilation be ordered at once."
translations.idiomatic: Let compilation be ordered at once."

sentences.zh: 六年，遷散騎常侍，又領徐州大中正，轉正員常侍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Regular Cavalry Attendant, also served as Senior Arbiter for Xuzhou, and was transferred to full Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to regular cavalry attendant, also served as senior arbiter for Xuzhou, and was made full regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 時有風雹為災，廣獻書高祖曰：「風雹變未必為災，古之聖賢輒懼而修己，所以興政化而隆德教也。

translations.literal: At that time wind and hail became a disaster; Guang presented a memorial to Gaozu, saying: "Wind and hail anomalies are not necessarily disasters; the sages and worthies of old always feared them and cultivated themselves — thereby they raised government and exalted moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and hail became disaster; Guang memorialized Gaozu: "Wind and hail anomalies are not necessarily disasters; sages of old always feared them and cultivated themselves — thereby they raised government and exalted moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 嘗忝服事，宿眷未忘，思竭塵露，率誠于習。

translations.literal: I once had the honor to serve you; old favor is not forgotten, and I wish to exhaust the dust and dew of my person and offer my utmost sincerity in what I have learned.
translations.idiomatic: I once served you; old favor is not forgotten, and I wish to exhaust my slight strength and offer my utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 明公初建義旗，匡複宗社，神武應運，信宿平夷。

translations.literal: When you first raised the banner of righteousness and restored the ancestral temple, divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, and within a night or two peace was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When you first raised the banner of righteousness and restored the ancestral temple, divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, and within a night or two peace was restored.

sentences.zh: 且恭儉謙約，虛心匪懈，來蘇之化，功用若神。

translations.literal: Moreover you are respectful, frugal, modest, and unwearying in open-mindedness; the transforming influence of "coming to renewal" works with godlike effect.
translations.idiomatic: You are respectful, frugal, modest, and unwearying in open-mindedness; the transforming influence of renewal works with godlike effect.

sentences.zh: 頃事故既多，刑德並用，戰功殷積，報敘難盡，萬機繁湊，固應難速，且小細煩密，群下多懼。

translations.literal: Recently affairs have been many, punishment and virtue employed together, battle achievements piled high and rewards hard to exhaust, the myriad tasks dense and pressing — it is naturally hard to be swift; moreover petty details are intricate and many below are fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Recently affairs have multiplied, punishment and virtue are employed together, battle achievements have piled up and rewards are hard to exhaust, the myriad tasks are dense — swiftness is naturally difficult; petty details are intricate and many below are fearful.

sentences.zh: 又谷帛豐賤，而民情不勸；

translations.literal: Moreover grain and silk are abundant and cheap, yet the people's hearts are not encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: Grain and silk are abundant and cheap, yet the people's hearts are not encouraged;

sentences.zh: 禁司互設，而劫盜多有，誠由俗弊未易整，而望深未易炳。

translations.literal: prohibitory offices are set up in mutual rivalry, yet banditry is frequent — truly because popular abuses are not easily rectified and expectations run deep and are not easily made clear.
translations.idiomatic: prohibitory offices multiply, yet banditry is frequent — truly because popular abuses are hard to rectify and deep expectations are hard to make clear.

sentences.zh: 追思義熙之始，如有不同，何者？

translations.literal: Reflecting on the beginning of Yixi, if there is any difference, what is it?
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on Yixi's beginning, if anything differs, what is it?

sentences.zh: 好安願逸，萬物之大趣，習舊駭新，凡識所不免。

translations.literal: Love of ease and wish for rest are the great bent of all things; habituating the old and fearing the new is what every understanding cannot avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Love of ease and wish for rest are the great bent of all things; habituating the old and fearing the new no understanding can avoid.

sentences.zh: 要當俯順群情，抑揚隨俗，則朝野歡泰，具瞻允康矣。

translations.literal: What is essential is to bow to the feelings of the multitude and moderate and follow custom — then court and countryside will rejoice in peace and all eyes will rest in true well-being.
translations.idiomatic: One must bow to the feelings of the multitude and moderate and follow custom — then court and countryside will rejoice and all eyes will rest in well-being.

sentences.zh: 言無可采，願矜其愚款之志。

translations.literal: My words have nothing worth adopting; I only ask that you regard my earnest and sincere intent.
translations.idiomatic: My words have nothing worth adopting; I only ask that you regard my earnest intent.

sentences.zh: 」又轉大司農，領著作郎皆如故。

translations.literal: " He was again transferred to Minister of Public Works, continuing as Compiler as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He was again transferred to minister of public works, continuing as compiler as before.

sentences.zh: 十二年，《晉紀》成，凡四十六卷，表上之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Jin Annals were completed — forty-six scrolls in all — and presented in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Jin Annals were completed — forty-six scrolls in all — and presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，桓玄篡位，安帝出宮，廣陪列悲慟，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An left the palace, Guang in the ranks grieved and was moved; sorrow moved those left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped and Emperor An left the palace, Guang in the ranks grieved; sorrow moved those beside him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，恭帝遜位，廣又哀感，涕泗交流。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang again was moved to sorrow and wept with flowing tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received abdication and Emperor Gong yielded, Guang again wept with flowing tears.

sentences.zh: 謝晦見之，謂之曰：「徐公將無小過？

translations.literal: Xie Hui, seeing this, said to him: "Master Xu will perhaps have a small fault?
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, seeing this, said, "Master Xu will perhaps have a small fault?

sentences.zh: 」廣收淚答曰：「身與君不同。

translations.literal: " Guang wiped his tears and answered: "My person and you are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang wiped his tears: "You and I are not the same.

sentences.zh: 君佐命興王，逢千載嘉運；

translations.literal: You assisted the mandate and raised the king, meeting a thousand-year auspicious fortune;
translations.idiomatic: You assisted the mandate and raised the king, meeting a thousand-year fortune;

sentences.zh: 身世荷晉德，實眷戀故主。

translations.literal: my person and generation owe Jin virtue and truly cherish attachment to the former lord.
translations.idiomatic: I owe Jin virtue and truly cherish my former lord.

sentences.zh: 」因更歔欷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sobbed again.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed again.

sentences.zh: 傅隆，字伯祚，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Long, styled Bozuo, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Long, styled Bozuo, was from Lingzhou in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 高祖咸，晉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xian (咸) was Metropolitan Commandant under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xian was Jin metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 曾祖晞，司徒屬。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xi (晞) was an aide in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xi was an aide in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父祖早亡。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father and grandfather died early.

sentences.zh: 隆少孤，又無近屬，單貧有學行，不好交遊。

translations.literal: Long was orphaned young and had no close kin; alone and poor, he possessed learning and conduct and did not care for socializing.
translations.idiomatic: Long was orphaned young and had no close kin; poor and alone, he possessed learning and conduct and did not care for socializing.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，年四十，始為孟昶建威將軍，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, at age forty, he first became Supernumerary Attendant Cavalry Gentleman on the staff of Meng Chang, General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: At Yixi's start, at age forty, he first became supernumerary attendant cavalry gentleman on Meng Chang's staff as general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 坐辭兼，免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for declining a concurrent post.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for declining a concurrent post.

sentences.zh: 複為會稽征虜參軍。

translations.literal: He again served as staff officer to the Pacifying Campaign in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as pacifying campaign staff officer in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 家在上虞，及東歸，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: His family was in Shangyu; when he returned east he formed the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: His family was in Shangyu; when he returned east he resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 曆佐三軍，首尾八年。

translations.literal: He successively served on three armies' staffs, eight years from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: He served on three armies' staffs in succession, eight years from first to last.

sentences.zh: 除給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed gentleman attendant at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射、丹陽尹徐羨之置建威府，以為錄事參軍，尋轉尚書祠部郎、丹陽丞，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Interior and Administrator of Danyang Xu Xianzhi established an Establishing Might office and made him recording secretary; soon he was transferred to Senior Clerk of Rites in the Interior and Vice Magistrate of Danyang, then entered service as Left Vice Director of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: Vice minister Xu Xianzhi established an establishing might office and made him recording secretary; soon he was senior clerk of rites, vice magistrate of Danyang, then left vice director of the interior.

sentences.zh: 以族弟亮為僕射，緦服不得相臨，徙太子率更令，廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍，出補山陰令。

translations.literal: Because his cousin Liang was vice minister, in distant mourning they could not face each other in office; he was moved to Director of the Heir Apparent's Household of Rate and Measure, staff adviser to Prince of Luling Liu Yizhen's chariots and cavalry, and sent out to fill the post of magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Because his cousin Liang was vice minister, in distant mourning they could not face each other in office; he was moved to the heir apparent's director of rate and measure, staff adviser to Prince of Luling Liu Yizhen, and sent out as magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉初，除司徒右長史，遷禦史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Secretariat and promoted to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanjia's start he was appointed right chief clerk of the secretariat and promoted to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 當官而行，甚得司直之體。

translations.literal: He acted according to his office and very much embodied the upright censor's manner.
translations.idiomatic: He acted according to his office and very much embodied the upright censor's manner.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left chief clerk of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時會稽剡縣民黃初妻趙打息載妻王死亡，遇赦，王有父母及息男稱、息女葉，依法徙趙二千裏外。

translations.literal: At that time in Yan County of Kuaiji, the commoner Huang Chu's wife Zhao beat to death Zai's wife Wang; there was an amnesty. Wang had parents and a son Cheng and a daughter Ye; by law Zhao was to be exiled two thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan county of Kuaiji, Huang Chu's wife Zhao beat Zai's wife Wang to death; there was an amnesty. Wang had parents and a son Cheng and daughter Ye; by law Zhao was to be exiled two thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 隆議之曰：「原夫禮律之興，蓋本之自然，求之情理，非從天墮，非從地出也。

translations.literal: Long debated the case, saying: "Tracing it to the root, the rise of ritual and law springs from what is natural and seeks what accords with principle — it did not fall from Heaven or spring from Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Long debated the case: "Ritual and law spring from nature and seek principle — they did not fall from Heaven or spring from Earth.

sentences.zh: 父子至親，分形同氣，稱之於載，即載之于趙，雖雲三世，為體猶一，未有能分之者也。

translations.literal: Father and son are utmost kin; they share form and share breath. Cheng toward Zai is what Zai is toward Zhao; though called three generations, as a body they are still one — there has never been anyone who could divide them.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son are utmost kin; they share form and breath. Cheng toward Zai is what Zai is toward Zhao; though called three generations, as one body they cannot be divided.

sentences.zh: 稱雖創巨痛深，固無仇祖之義。

translations.literal: Though Cheng suffers wound beyond measure and pain beyond depth, he certainly has no principle of avenging a grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cheng's wound is beyond measure, he has no principle of avenging a grandmother.

sentences.zh: 若稱可以殺趙，趙當何以處載？

translations.literal: If Cheng may kill Zhao, how should Zhao treat Zai?
translations.idiomatic: If Cheng may kill Zhao, how should Zhao treat Zai?

sentences.zh: 將父子孫祖，互相殘戮，懼非先王明罰，咎繇立法之本旨也。

translations.literal: To have father, son, grandson, and grandfather mutually slaughter one another — I fear this is not the intent of the former kings' clear punishments and Gao Yao's establishment of law.
translations.idiomatic: Father, son, grandson, and grandfather mutually slaughtering one another — I fear this is not the intent of the former kings' clear punishments and Gao Yao's law.

sentences.zh: 向使石厚之子、日磾之孫，砥鋒挺鍔，不與二祖同戴天日，則石碏、秺侯何得流名百代，以為美談者哉！

translations.literal: Suppose the son of Shi Hou and the grandson of Ri Di had whetted blades and drawn swords and did not share Heaven and sun with the two ancestors — how could Shi Que and the Marquis of Di have left their names for a hundred generations as subjects of fine renown!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Shi Hou's son and Ri Di's grandson had drawn swords and did not share Heaven and sun with the two ancestors — how could Shi Que and the Marquis of Di have left their names for a hundred generations as fine renown!

sentences.zh: 舊令雲，'殺人父母，徙之二千裏外'。

translations.literal: The old statute says, "Those who kill another's parents are exiled two thousand li away."
translations.idiomatic: The old statute says, "Those who kill another's parents are exiled two thousand li away."

sentences.zh: 不施父子孫祖明矣。

translations.literal: That it does not apply to father, son, grandson, and grandfather is clear.
translations.idiomatic: That it does not apply to father, son, grandson, and grandfather is clear.

sentences.zh: 趙當避王期功千里外耳。

translations.literal: Zhao need only avoid Wang's mourning circle of one year and mutual mourning at a distance of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao need only avoid Wang's mourning circle at a distance of a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 令亦雲，'凡流徙者，同籍親近欲相隨者，聽之'。

translations.literal: The statute also says, "For all who are exiled, if those of the same register who are close kin wish to follow, they are permitted."
translations.idiomatic: The statute also says, "For all who are exiled, if close kin of the same register wish to follow, they are permitted."

sentences.zh: 此又大通情體，因親以教愛者也。

translations.literal: This again greatly accords with feeling and principle — teaching love through kinship.
translations.idiomatic: This again accords with feeling and principle — teaching love through kinship.

sentences.zh: 趙既流移，載為人子，何得不從；

translations.literal: Since Zhao is exiled, Zai as a son — how can he not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhao is exiled, Zai as a son — how can he not follow?

sentences.zh: 載從而稱不行，豈名教所許？

translations.literal: If Zai follows yet Cheng does not go, is that what name and teaching permit?
translations.idiomatic: If Zai follows yet Cheng does not go, is that what name and teaching permit?

sentences.zh: 如此，稱、趙竟不可分。

translations.literal: Thus Cheng and Zhao in the end cannot be separated.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Cheng and Zhao cannot be separated.

sentences.zh: 趙雖內愧終身，稱當沈痛沒齒，孫祖之義，自不得永絕，事理固然也。

translations.literal: Though Zhao will bear inner shame all her life, Cheng should grieve to the marrow until his teeth are gone; the righteousness of grandson and grandfather cannot be cut off forever — in principle and fact it is necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhao will bear inner shame all her life, Cheng should grieve to the marrow; the righteousness of grandson and grandfather cannot be cut off — in principle it is necessarily so.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " They followed his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: They followed his opinion.

sentences.zh: 又出為義興太守，在郡有能名。

translations.literal: He was again sent out as Administrator of Yixing and won a reputation for competence in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as administrator of Yixing and won a reputation for competence in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 征拜左民尚書，坐正直受節假，對人未至，委出，白衣領職。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of the Left for the People; for integrity he received leave with seal, yet when the person he was to meet had not arrived he left his post on his own — he retained office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of the left for the people; for integrity he received leave with seal, yet when the person he was to meet had not arrived he left on his own — he retained office in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太常。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太祖以新撰《禮論》付隆使下意，隆上表曰：「臣以下愚，不涉師訓，孤陋閭閻，面牆靡識，謬蒙詢逮，愧懼流汗。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Emperor Wen entrusted to Long the newly compiled Ritual Discussions for him to convey their intent; Long submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant, being low and foolish, has not undergone teachers' instruction; alone and narrow in the lanes, facing the wall I have no knowledge — wrongly favored with inquiry, I sweat with shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Emperor Wen entrusted the newly compiled Ritual Discussions to Long to convey their intent; Long memorialized: "Your servant, low and foolish, has not undergone teachers' instruction; alone in the lanes, facing the wall I have no knowledge — wrongly favored with inquiry, I sweat with shame.

sentences.zh: 原夫禮者，三千之本，人倫之至道。

translations.literal: Tracing it to the root, ritual is the foundation of the three thousand rules and the utmost Way of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is the foundation of the three thousand rules and the utmost Way of human relations.

sentences.zh: 故用之家國，君臣以之尊，父子以之親；

translations.literal: Therefore in employing it in state and family, lord and minister thereby gain honor, father and son thereby gain closeness;
translations.idiomatic: Employed in state and family, lord and minister thereby gain honor, father and son thereby gain closeness;

sentences.zh: 用之婚冠，少長以之仁愛，夫妻以之義順；

translations.literal: employed in marriage and capping, young and old thereby gain humane love, husband and wife thereby gain righteous harmony;
translations.idiomatic: employed in marriage and capping, young and old thereby gain humane love, husband and wife thereby gain righteous harmony;

sentences.zh: 用之鄉人，友朋以之三益，賓主以之敬讓。

translations.literal: employed among village fellows, friends thereby gain the three benefits, host and guest thereby gain respect and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: employed among village fellows, friends thereby gain the three benefits, host and guest thereby gain respect and yielding.

sentences.zh: 所謂極乎天，播乎地，窮高遠，測深厚，莫尚於禮也。

translations.literal: What is called reaching to Heaven, spreading over Earth, probing the far and high, measuring the deep and thick — nothing surpasses ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching to Heaven, spreading over Earth, probing the far and high, measuring the deep and thick — nothing surpasses ritual.

sentences.zh: 其樂之五聲，《易》之八象，《詩》之《風雅》，《書》之《典誥》，《春秋》之微婉勸懲，無不本乎禮而後立也。

translations.literal: The five tones of music, the eight trigrams of the Changes, the Feng and Ya of the Odes, the Dian and Gao of the Documents, the subtle remonstrance and encouragement of the Spring and Autumn Annals — none fails to take ritual as root and only then stand.
translations.idiomatic: The five tones of music, the eight trigrams of the Changes, the Feng and Ya of the Odes, the Dian and Gao of the Documents, the subtle remonstrance of the Spring and Autumn Annals — none fails to take ritual as root and then stand.

sentences.zh: 其源遠，其流廣，其體大，其義精，非夫睿哲大賢，孰能明乎此哉。

translations.literal: Its source is distant, its flow broad, its body great, its meaning refined — unless a sage of penetrating wisdom, who can clarify this?
translations.idiomatic: Its source is distant, its flow broad, its body great, its meaning refined — unless a sage of penetrating wisdom, who can clarify this?

sentences.zh: 況遭暴秦焚亡，百不存一。

translations.literal: Moreover it suffered the violent Qin's burning and perishing; not one in a hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it suffered the violent Qin's burning; not one in a hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 漢興，始徵召故老，搜集殘文，其體例紕繆，首尾脫落，難可詳論。

translations.literal: When Han rose, it first summoned old worthies and gathered surviving texts; the form and examples were tangled, beginning and end fell away — hard to discuss in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, it summoned old worthies and gathered surviving texts; form and examples were tangled, beginning and end fell away — hard to discuss in detail.

sentences.zh: 幸高堂生頗識舊義，諸儒各為章句之說，既明不獨達，所見不同，或師資相傳，共枝別幹。

translations.literal: Fortunately Gao Tang Sheng knew well the old meaning; the various Confucians each made chapter-and-sentence explanations — since understanding did not reach alone, what they saw differed, or master and pupil handed down and branched into separate stems.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tang Sheng knew the old meaning; the Confucians each made chapter-and-sentence explanations — understanding did not reach alone, what they saw differed, or master and pupil handed down and branched into separate stems.

sentences.zh: 故聞人、二戴，俱事後蒼，俄已分異；

translations.literal: Thus Wen and the two Dai, both studying under Hou Cang, soon diverged;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wen and the two Dai, both studying under Hou Cang, soon diverged;

sentences.zh: 盧植、鄭玄，偕學馬融，人各名象。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan, together studying under Ma Rong, each made a name with his own standards.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan, together studying under Ma Rong, each made a name with his own standards.

sentences.zh: 又後之學者，未逮曩時，而問難星繁，充斥兼兩，摛文列錦，煥爛可觀。

translations.literal: Moreover later scholars did not reach former times, yet questioning and debate multiplied like stars, filling more than two carriage-loads; composing texts arrayed like brocade, splendid and worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Later scholars did not reach former times, yet debate multiplied like stars, filling more than two carriage-loads; texts arrayed like brocade, splendid and worth viewing.

sentences.zh: 然而五服之本或差，哀敬之制舛雜，國典未一于四海，家法參駁於縉紳，誠宜考詳遠慮，以定皇代之盛禮者也。

translations.literal: Yet the root of the five garments of mourning was sometimes wrong, and systems of mourning and respect were mixed and confused; the national canon was not unified throughout the four seas, and household law was at odds among the gentry — truly one should examine in detail and think far ahead to fix the flourishing ritual of the imperial age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the root of the five garments of mourning was sometimes wrong, and systems of mourning and respect were confused; the national canon was not unified, and household law was at odds among the gentry — one should examine in detail and fix the flourishing ritual of the imperial age.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下欽明玄聖，同規唐、虞，疇咨四嶽，興言《三禮》，而伯夷未登，微臣竊位，所以大懼負乘，形神交惡者，無忘夙夜矣。

translations.literal: Bow your head: Your Majesty is reverent, bright, and mysteriously sage, sharing the standards of Tang and Yu, consulting the four mountains, raising discourse on the Three Rites — yet Bo Yi has not ascended and your low servant wrongly holds his post; therefore the great fear of the overloaded cart and the affliction of body and spirit — do not forget day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is reverent, bright, and mysteriously sage, sharing the standards of Tang and Yu, consulting the four mountains, raising discourse on the Three Rites — yet Bo Yi has not ascended and your low servant wrongly holds his post; therefore great fear of the overloaded cart — do not forget day and night.

sentences.zh: 而複猥充搏采之數，與聞爰發之求，實無以仰酬聖旨萬分之一。

translations.literal: Yet again I am wrongly placed among those who gather and select, and heard in the search that was sent forth — truly I have no means to repay the sage intent even one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet again I am wrongly placed among those who gather and select — truly I have no means to repay the sage intent even one ten-thousandth.

sentences.zh: 不敢廢默，謹率管穴所見五十二事上呈。

translations.literal: I dare not remain silent and waste words; I respectfully lead forth fifty-two matters seen through a tube's aperture and present them above.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not remain silent; I respectfully submit fifty-two points drawn from my narrow understanding.

sentences.zh: 蚩鄙茫浪，伏用竦赧。」

translations.literal: Ignorant, coarse, vast and confused, I prostrate myself and am struck with shame."
translations.idiomatic: Crude and confused as I am, I prostrate myself in shame."

sentences.zh: 明年，致仕，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired and was appointed grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 歸老在家，手不釋卷，博學多通，特精《三禮》。

translations.literal: He returned home in old age, never releasing a scroll from his hand; broadly learned and master of much, he was especially skilled in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home in old age and never put down his books; broadly learned and accomplished in many fields, he was especially expert in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 謹于奉公，常手抄書籍。

translations.literal: Careful in serving the public, he often copied books by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Conscientious in public service, he often copied books by hand.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，時年八十三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died, at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：選賢於野，則治身業弘；

translations.literal: The historian says: When worthies are chosen in the wilds, then self-cultivation and enterprise are broad;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: When worthies are chosen in the countryside, self-cultivation and public service flourish;

sentences.zh: 求士子朝，則飾智風起。

translations.literal: when scholars are sought at court, then the wind of adorned cleverness rises.
translations.idiomatic: when scholars are sought at court, the fashion for display and cleverness rises.

sentences.zh: 《六經》奧遠，方軌之正路；

translations.literal: The Six Classics are profound and far-reaching — the correct road of the square track;
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics are profound and far-reaching — the true highway of learning;

sentences.zh: 百家淺末，捷至之偏道。

translations.literal: the hundred schools shallow and marginal — the side path of quick arrival.
translations.idiomatic: the hundred schools shallow and marginal — a shortcut bypath.

sentences.zh: 漢世登士，閭黨為先，崇本務學，不尚浮詭，然後可以俯拾青組，顧蔑籝金。

translations.literal: In Han times to rise as scholar, village and district came first; honoring the root and devoting to learning, not esteeming floating trickery — only then could one stoop to pick up blue cords and look down on chests of gold.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times advancement depended first on village and district reputation; honoring fundamentals and devoting oneself to learning, not prizing flashy cleverness — only then could one readily gain office and disdain mere wealth.

sentences.zh: 於是人厲從師之志，家競專門之術，藝重當時，所居一旦成市，黌舍暫啟，著錄或至萬人。

translations.literal: Thus people sharpened the will to follow teachers, families competed in specialized arts; craft was weighty in the age — where one dwelt became a market in a day; when schoolhouses briefly opened, those registered sometimes reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thus people sharpened their resolve to follow teachers, and families competed in specialized disciplines; learning was honored in the age — a master's residence could become a marketplace overnight, and when academies opened, enrollment sometimes reached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 是故仕以學成，身由義立。

translations.literal: Therefore office came through learning completed, the person established through righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore office came through completed learning, and personal standing through established righteousness.

sentences.zh: 自魏氏膺命，主愛雕蟲，家棄章句，人重異術。

translations.literal: From the time Wei received the mandate, lords loved ornamental writing, families abandoned clause and comment, people valued strange arts.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Wei received the mandate, rulers loved ornamental writing, families abandoned textual commentary, and people prized unorthodox arts.

sentences.zh: 又選賢進士，不本鄉閭，銓衡之寄，任歸台閣。

translations.literal: Again in selecting worthies and advancing scholars, one did not base on village and hamlet; the trust of weighing and balancing rested with the terrace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in selecting worthies and advancing scholars, local community was no longer the basis; the power of evaluation rested with the central offices.

sentences.zh: 以一人之耳目，究山川之險情，賢否臆斷，萬不值一。

translations.literal: With one person's ears and eyes to exhaust the dangerous conditions of mountains and rivers, judging worthy or not by guess — not one in ten thousand hit true.
translations.idiomatic: With one person's senses to judge the hidden conditions of every region, worthiness was guessed at — scarcely one judgment in ten thousand was correct.

sentences.zh: 由是仕憑藉譽，學非為己，崇詭遇之巧速，鄙稅駕之遲難，士自此委笥植《經》，各從所務，早往晏退，以取世資。

translations.literal: Hence office relied on borrowed fame, learning was not for oneself; they honored the clever speed of chance encounter and despised the slow difficulty of mounting the carriage — scholars from this stored cases and planted the classics, each following his business, going early and returning late to seize worldly resources.
translations.idiomatic: Hence office relied on borrowed reputation and learning was not pursued for its own sake; clever opportunism was honored and patient thoroughness despised — scholars stored their classics in boxes, each pursued his own affairs, and went early and left late to gain worldly advantage.

sentences.zh: 庠序黌校之士，傳經聚徒之業，自黃初至於晉末，百餘年中，儒教盡矣。

translations.literal: The scholars of village schools and academies, the enterprise of transmitting classics and gathering disciples — from Huangchu to the end of Jin, more than a hundred years, Confucian teaching was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars of village schools and academies, the work of transmitting the classics and gathering disciples — from Huangchu to the end of Jin, for more than a hundred years, Confucian teaching was spent.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，議創國學，宮車早晏，道未及行。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the mandate, they debated founding a National University; the imperial carriage departed early, and the Way had not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received the mandate, they debated founding a National University, but he died before the plan could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 迄於元嘉，甫獲克就，雅風盛烈，未及曩時，而濟濟焉，頗有前王之遺典。

translations.literal: Down to Yuanjia it was at last achieved; elegant wind and flourishing splendor did not reach former times, yet abundantly there were somewhat the former kings' surviving canons.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuanjia era it was at last achieved; its elegant culture, though not equal to former ages, was nonetheless abundant and preserved much of the former kings' legacy.

sentences.zh: 天子鸞旗警蹕，清道而臨學館，儲後冕旒黼黻，北面而禮先師，後生所不嘗聞，黃發未之前睹，亦一代之盛也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven with imperial banners and cleared road came to the academy; the heir apparent in cap-strings and embroidered robes faced north and paid ritual to the former master — what later students had never heard, what white-haired elders had never before seen; this too was a splendor of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, banners flying and roads cleared, came to the academy; the heir apparent in full regalia faced north to honor the former master — what younger generations had never heard and white-haired elders had never seen — this too was a glory of the age.

sentences.zh: 臧燾、徐廣、傅隆、裴松之、何承天、雷次宗，並服膺聖哲，不為雅俗推移，立名於世，宜矣。

translations.literal: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all embraced the sages in their breasts, were not shifted by refined or vulgar custom, and established names in the world — fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all embraced the sages in their hearts, were not swayed by fashionable opinion, and established lasting reputations — as was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 潁川庾蔚之、雁門周野王、汝南周王子、河內向琰、會稽賀道養，皆托志經書，見稱於後學。

translations.literal: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all entrusted their aims to the classics and were praised by later students.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all devoted themselves to the classics and were praised by later scholars.

sentences.zh: 蔚之略解《禮記》，並注賀循《喪服》，行於世雲。

translations.literal: Weizhi had a summary understanding of the Book of Rites and also annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments — it circulated in the world, they say.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi had a summary grasp of the Book of Rites and also annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments — both circulated in his day.
